reasons.A: Closest movement: long semicolon-linked periods broken by short plain sentences, double-dash asides, and a gently self-mocking, confiding stance like the passage's; the run of similes edges slightly towards imitation.
reasons.B: Right period register and wry tone, and the closing exclamation fits the author, but the sentences are heavier and more uniformly periodic, and the personified Nature and 'jewelled' flourish lay the manner on a little thick.
reasons.C: Modern, plain, explanatory prose with even mid-length sentences, almost no semicolons or dashes and a present-day register; it has none of the author's cadence or whimsy.
